candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On 'the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God' (Deu 4:24), Ephrem reads the doubled-image (consuming fire + jealous God) as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of Hebrews 12:29 ('for our God is a consuming fire' — verbatim citation). The fire-image is not destructive wrath but the purifying jealousy that refuses rival affections. Tewahedo theology cites Deu 4:24 + Heb 12:29 as the canonical doubled-witness that the encounter-with-God is always simultaneously consoling and consuming; the Eucharist itself receives the same description in the Tewahedo Anaphora of Athanasius: 'this is the burning coal which Isaiah saw'.
